public_rationale: The reported 48% increase is supported. The full causal claim is not settled. Google's disclosure identifies data-center energy use and supply-chain emissions, but does not isolate AI's contribution. Nor does one company's increase establish a massive worldwide effect. Missing attribution is not evidence that AI had no effect, so it does not justify contradiction or a mixed grade.
limitations: The numerical component is stronger than the causal and worldwide components.
The sources do not provide a causal decomposition.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Artificial intelligence, driven by generative AI, is already massively increasing global emissions, particularly from companies like Google, whose emissions rose 48% in the last five years thanks to AI.

statement.excerpt: Even if changing this were possible — and it'd be good for society if it was — artificial intelligence (driven by generative AI) is already massively increasing global emissions, particularly from companies like Google, which saw its emissions increase by 48% in the last five years thanks to AI.

from_speaker: emissions increase by 48% in the last five years
our_interpretation: Assess the reported 2019–2023 emissions comparison, the five annual observations underlying the report available before the post.
Read thanks to AI as asserting a substantial causal contribution, without requiring AI to be the only cause.
Read massively increasing global emissions as a substantial worldwide emissions effect, not merely higher electricity use or a large percentage change at one company.
Treat the numerical increase and its causal attribution as separate components.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence confirms Google's approximately 48% increase from 2019 to 2023 and establishes that AI materially caused it, alongside a substantial worldwide emissions increase attributable to AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable emissions records refute the reported increase, or credible attribution evidence establishes that AI did not materially cause the asserted corporate and worldwide increases.
